proposals.title: A large breakfast
proposals.body: I started down the side of a sea squirt taller than I am. At this size, lunch has terrain.
proposals.reason: The source explicitly labels a juvenile N. kubaryana; the animal is visibly small beside a tall translucent ascidian. Its pale narrow stripes and blue bases differ strongly from the chosen adult. The 2023 colour-ontogeny paper examines other Nembrotha species and must not be used to certify this exact juvenile. Keep this proposed childhood scene held for a stronger species/age corroboration. No bite is resolved; the prose treats the substrate as potential food, not a recorded meal.

proposals.title: Breakfast is fastened down
proposals.body: I put my face into the blue colony and stopped traveling. Every mouthful left more breakfast attached to the rock.
proposals.reason: A fully identified Anilao N. kubaryana runs head-down beside a pale sponge, with its mouth at a blue ascidian colony. The prey remains attached. The actual contact, food field and posture support the event; do not identify the ascidian to species or claim this particular meal was chemically assayed.

proposals.title: Plenty of room
proposals.body: There is room for both of us here. We have managed to use the same part.
proposals.reason: Two identified Anilao animals crowd the same patch of pale green ascidians. The bodies meet and one head faces toward the viewer. The image is strong, but the scene overlaps the stronger two-mouth feeding proposal for slot 7. Do not admit both merely because they have different hashes.

proposals.title: All of me must turn
proposals.body: I took the corner headfirst. My gills are still on the old side of the rock. We are both insisting this is forward.
proposals.reason: One identified animal curls tightly around the edge of a rock, head below and gills away at left. The awkward bent body supplies the joke. No snail, current or forced backward movement is invented. The original is only 640 by 480 and visibly softer than the Delso images; lead should decide whether the unusually clear action outweighs that limitation.

proposals.title: Nothing elsewhere
proposals.body: I have my mouth against one clump of sea squirts and another waiting beside me. My gills are open. Nothing needs me anywhere else.
proposals.reason: Source explicitly records N. kubaryana feeding on tunicates in East Timor. A close detailed image shows mouth against a clump, another clump at right and fully spread gills. Visually excellent, but its settled feeding event repeats slot 2. Reserve as a replacement option for slot 2 if the lead prefers this exact view; do not pad the arc with both.

proposals.title: Separate mouths
proposals.body: They came at the colony from above. I came from the side. We have made an agreement entirely out of mouths.
proposals.reason: Two N. kubaryana press their mouths to adjacent clumps of the same tunicate colony, one from above and one from left. The source explicitly identifies feeding. This is cooperative appetite rather than another mating joke. The file says Clavelina; prose deliberately stays at colony because prey taxonomy is not needed for the joke. This replaces the excluded egg scene with a different real event, not false maternity.

proposals.title: Under the edge
proposals.body: The roof has my tail. My head is looking for the floor. I would like the next part of the reef to be somewhere I can put myself.
proposals.reason: An identified Dumaguete N. kubaryana hangs sharply down from an overhang, rear attached beneath its upper edge and head extended into open space. No predator or fall is invented. The posture is a downward search beneath a ledge, distinct from the horizontal crossing in slot 9.

proposals.title: One foot, several problems
proposals.body: I left my tail on one side of the lump and stretched my face toward the other. For a creature with one foot, I have made this unnecessarily complicated.
proposals.reason: One identified animal stretches across an uneven rounded substrate, front projecting left and rear draped down the right, leaving a dark gap beneath its front/middle. The muscular foot is one continuous organ; the story concerns managing body length across this particular obstruction. No snail climbs over it and no current folds it.
